title: What's Biting
region: Texas bays, written for the Galveston Bay area
note: Typical patterns, not a promise. Cold fronts, rain, and water temperature can move fish a few weeks early or late.

seasons.where: Deep holes, channels, bayous, and soft mud with scattered shell. On sunny afternoons after a front, they slide onto shallow mud flats to warm up.
seasons.bait: Slow-sinking twitchbaits and soft plastics on light jigheads, worked very slowly.
seasons.tip: February is known for big trout around Galveston. Fish the warm days between cold fronts, and slow way down when the water is in the low 50s.

seasons.where: Moving from winter spots to shorelines, shell reefs, and grass as the water warms. Prime time for a trophy trout.
seasons.bait: Soft plastics, topwaters as it warms up, and live shrimp once bait shops have it again.
seasons.tip: Find bait like mullet or shad along the shoreline. Big trout won't be far away.

seasons.where: Shallow shorelines and grass early and late. In the heat of the day, deeper reefs, drop-offs, gas wells, the jetties, and the surf when it's calm and green.
seasons.bait: Live shrimp or small croaker, and soft plastics.
seasons.tip: Go at first light. By midday, move to deeper water near structure.

seasons.where: Under diving gulls in open water as shrimp leave the marsh, mostly October and November. Also on shorelines and reefs as the water cools.
seasons.bait: Shrimp-style soft plastics under the birds, or live shrimp under a cork.
seasons.tip: Best a day or two after a cool front. Trout under the birds are often small; bigger ones tend to hold along shorelines.

seasons.where: Bayous, tidal creeks, rivers, and mud flats close to deep water. Cold snaps push lots of reds up the creeks.
seasons.bait: Cut mullet or shrimp on the bottom, or soft plastics worked slowly.
seasons.tip: On cold mornings, wait for the afternoon sun to warm the shallows.

seasons.where: Back on shallow shorelines, marsh edges, and oyster reefs as the water warms.
seasons.bait: Gold spoons, soft plastics, and live or fresh shrimp.
seasons.tip: Watch for wakes and tails in skinny water and cast past them.

seasons.where: Shallow flats and marsh drains early, reefs and deeper edges at midday. By late August, big bull reds start gathering near the passes.
seasons.bait: Live shrimp, finger mullet, small crabs, and spoons.
seasons.tip: Fish marsh drains on a moving tide, when bait gets flushed out.

seasons.where: Bull reds at the jetties, passes, and surf in September and October. Slot reds work marsh drains on falling tides and sometimes school under birds.
seasons.bait: Cut mullet, live mullet, or blue crab for bull reds. Shrimp, spoons, and soft plastics in the bay.
seasons.tip: Bull reds are over the 28-inch slot, so release them unless you use your Red Drum Tag. Circle hooks make releasing easy.

seasons.where: Most adults have left for the Gulf to spawn. Some stay in deep holes, harbors, and boat basins.
seasons.bait: Soft plastics on a jighead, dragged slowly along the bottom.
seasons.tip: Bites drop off once the water is in the 50s, but some big flounder stay around harbors.

seasons.where: Coming back into the bays from the Gulf. Check marsh drains, drop-offs, and pilings.
seasons.bait: Mud minnows, finger mullet, shrimp, or soft plastics on the bottom.
seasons.tip: Go slow. Flounder lie still and ambush bait instead of chasing it.

seasons.where: Spread out along marsh drains, shorelines, reefs, and pilings, on sandy or muddy edges.
seasons.bait: Mud minnows, finger mullet, shrimp, or scented soft plastics.
seasons.tip: Fish the edges where a falling tide washes bait out of the marsh.

seasons.where: Heading for the Gulf. They gather in channels, along the ship channel, and at the passes and jetties.
seasons.bait: Mud minnows, finger mullet, and soft plastics.
seasons.tip: A strong cold front can start a big push toward the passes. Check the closure dates before you keep any.

seasons.where: Deeper water: channels, the ship channel, jetties, and the surf. Big "bull" drum gather at the jetties and passes in late winter.
seasons.bait: Peeled shrimp, fresh crab with the shell off, or cut bait on the bottom.
seasons.tip: February and March are prime for big drum. Drum from 30 to 52 inches go back.

seasons.where: Big drum at the jetties and passes through March, then spreading through the bays on reefs and in channels.
seasons.bait: Peeled shrimp, fresh crab, or cut bait.
seasons.tip: They find food by smell, so fresh bait beats lures.

seasons.where: Schools of 1 to 4 pound drum in shallow water, around reefs, piers, and marsh edges.
seasons.bait: Peeled shrimp or pieces of crab.
seasons.tip: Feeding schools stir up muddy patches in clear water. Cast to the edge of the mud.

seasons.where: Reefs, channels, and piers, moving deeper as the water cools.
seasons.bait: Peeled shrimp or fresh crab.
seasons.tip: Smaller drum in the slot are the best eating.

seasons.where: Jetties, pilings, piers, docks, and rocks. They bunch up on structure as it gets cold.
seasons.bait: Live or fresh shrimp, fiddler crabs, or barnacles on a small hook.
seasons.tip: They nibble. Use a small, strong hook and set it at the first weight you feel.

seasons.where: Moving out the passes in groups to spawn. Fish the jetties and piers near the passes.
seasons.bait: Fiddler crabs or shrimp.
seasons.tip: March and April are the spawning run, the best time for big sheepshead.

seasons.where: Back on bay structure: pilings, docks, oyster reefs, and rigs. Fewer big ones.
seasons.bait: Shrimp, fiddler crabs, or barnacles.
seasons.tip: Fish right against the structure. A few feet away is too far.

seasons.where: Schools in deeper bay channels, the ship channel, and the passes.
seasons.bait: Dead shrimp or cut bait on the bottom, or small jigs.
seasons.tip: An easy fish for kids, with no size or bag limit.

seasons.where: Big schools in the channels and near the passes as they get ready to spawn.
seasons.bait: Shrimp, squid, or small jigs tipped with shrimp.
seasons.tip: Spawning peaks in spring near the passes, so this is the best time for numbers.

seasons.where: Many move offshore when the bay gets very hot. Try deep channels and nearshore structure.
seasons.bait: Dead shrimp on the bottom.
seasons.tip: Fish early, or at night under lights near the passes.

seasons.where: Back in the bays, often mixed in with trout under diving birds.
seasons.bait: Shrimp-style soft plastics or dead shrimp.
seasons.tip: They don't freeze well, so eat them fresh.

seasons.where: Most have left the bays for the Gulf. A few stay in the deepest channels.
seasons.bait: Small pieces of shrimp on the bottom.
seasons.tip: A slow time for croaker in the bay.

seasons.where: Back in the bays over soft, muddy bottom: channels, the Intracoastal, and piers.
seasons.bait: Small pieces of shrimp or squid on the bottom.
seasons.tip: Small live croaker are also top bait for big trout in summer.

seasons.where: Big croaker gather and head out through the passes to the Gulf, usually peaking in October. Try the channels, the Intracoastal, and the jetties.
seasons.bait: Shrimp or squid on the bottom.
seasons.tip: Old-timers say the croaker run comes just before the flounder run.

seasons.where: Few in the bays when the water is cold.
seasons.bait: Shrimp or cut bait on the bottom, if you're after them.
seasons.tip: Warm months are much better for gafftop.

seasons.where: Bays, channels, passes, and the surf, feeding near the bottom and higher up.
seasons.bait: Shrimp, cut mullet, small crabs, or pinfish.
seasons.tip: Males carry the eggs in their mouths in summer and may not eat for weeks. Watch the spines: sharp, with toxic slime.

seasons.where: Still in the bays and surf. Larger fish are common in fall.
seasons.bait: Cut mullet or shrimp.
seasons.tip: Use a strong hook and handle them with pliers or a towel.

seasons.where: Almost everywhere in the bay, especially on the bottom around piers and channels.
seasons.bait: They'll eat any natural bait you put on the bottom.
seasons.tip: To dodge them, use lures or float your bait off the bottom under a cork.

seasons.where: Usually far fewer around when the water is cold.
seasons.bait: Any natural bait.
seasons.tip: A good time for bottom fishing without the bait thieves.

seasons.where: Big schools leave the bays to spawn in the Gulf, late October through December, moving through the passes and along the beach.
seasons.bait: Prime time to throw a cast net for live or cut bait.
seasons.tip: Predators follow the run. Bull reds, trout, and flounder feed hard on mullet now.

seasons.where: Young mullet move into the marsh and back bays from January through May.
seasons.bait: Fewer bait-size mullet around until summer.
seasons.tip: The little ones in the marsh now will be finger mullet by summer.

seasons.where: Finger mullet along shorelines, marsh edges, and drains.
seasons.bait: Cast net them for live bait for trout, reds, and flounder.
seasons.tip: Hook a live finger mullet through the lips or behind the back fin. The Free-Lined rig works the same way as with shrimp.

seasons.where: Deep, protected water like the Brownsville Ship Channel and the South Padre and Boca Chica jetties.
seasons.bait: Live shrimp or mullet, or slow soft plastics.
seasons.tip: Snook can't handle cold water, so they hide deep when it gets cold.

seasons.where: Lower Laguna Madre shorelines, jetties, channels, and structure with strong current.
seasons.bait: Live shrimp or mullet, and soft plastics.
seasons.tip: Strong current and structure are the keys.
